critiques.summary: H1 is now well supported and the alternatives are contradicted by direct evidence. My round-1 blocking objection — that the causal claim rested on 4-minute bucket co-occurrence with an untested pre-12:04 onset — is closed: F25/F26/F27 show pricing-engine CPU flat 38.03–41.86% and p99 56.82–63.09ms in every 1-min bucket 11:50–12:04Z (the 12:04 bucket is the last clean one), stepping strictly to 98.65% / 2534.9ms at 12:05Z with zero GreeksV2 WARNs before 12:05:21Z, exactly one minute after the verified cfg-3120 ramp (rollout_pct 5→100 at 12:04:00Z). Ordering is tight: ramp 12:04Z → CPU/latency step 12:05Z → GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo WARN 12:05:21Z (6465–8361ms vs the 2000ms budget) → order-service client 2500ms timeout ERROR 12:06:10Z. Capacity loss is excluded (request_rate flat 591–687 req/s, restarts 0.0, memory 46–53%, F28), so the CPU step is added per-request algorithmic cost. H2 and H3 are now falsified, not just dismissed: redis hit-ratio/CPU/clients/evictions flat (F19/F20), market-data-service p99 36.5–42.3ms and error_rate 0.11–0.32% flat through its own 11:56Z protobuf deploy (F21/F22), and no protobuf/parse/schema message in pricing-engine logs (F23). The round-1 enumeration gap is closed (all-services config re-run returns count 1, partial:false, only cfg-3120; F32/F33), so no third-party change is hiding in the window. Remaining shortfalls are non-blocking: the decisive recovery-on-revert experiment is impossible because the flag was never reverted (F31/F33), and blast radius among other pricing-engine/market-data-service consumers is unmeasured. These justify a confidence cap, not a rank change or further rounds during an active outage.

challenges.issue: Decisive confirmation (recovery on revert) is absent: cfg-3120 was never reverted or re-changed through 13:59Z (F31/F33) and the in-window recovery half (did pricing-engine CPU/p99 and order-service error_rate ever fall in 12:04–13:59Z) was not verified. H1 therefore rests on a tight but purely circumstantial temporal correlation rather than a demonstrated cause-and-effect toggle.

Blast radius unmeasured: no other consumers of pricing-engine (portfolio-service, api-gateway) or market-data-service were checked, so it is unconfirmed that the degradation is an internal pricing-engine compute effect rather than something order-service-specific. This is consistent with H1 but not proven; it also leaves the H4 self-degradation path on weaker footing than it could be.

Provenance inconsistency: F20/F21/F22 (redis and market-data-service telemetry) are labelled UNVERIFIED even though the observability agent retrieved them in T5. The values are internally coherent, so this is a labelling defect, not a data-quality problem, but it means the redis/market-data contradiction of H2/H3 should be read as retrieved-but-unattested.

The report's framing ('shipped a serialization change a few minutes before') is factually wrong: the market-data-service deploy was ~8–10 minutes before onset (F13), and it shows zero latency/error step at its own deploy (F21/F22). The alternative is correctly rejected but the reporter's premise should not be relied on.
